info.description:
E-Commerce Payments Services API
The purpose of this document is to explain the use of the RestFUL Web Services for integration with PaymentN&TS GROUP E-Commerce Payments Services.

Message Signature
This topic describes how to sign API requests.

Summary of Signing Steps
These are the steps required to sign a request:
1) Form the HTTPS request.
2) Create the signing string, which is based on parts of the request.
3) Create the signature from the signing string using hmac-sha256 algorithm.
4) Add the resulting signature and other required information to the "Authorization" header in the request.

Specification You Need to Be Familiar With
To learn how to perform steps 2-4 in the process above, refer to https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-cavage-http-signatures-10. It's a draft specification that forms the basis for how request signatures are handled. It describes generally how to form the signing string, how to create the signature, and how to add the signature and required information to the request. The remaining sections in this topic assume you're familiar with it.

Implementation Details
[Authorization Header]
The "Signature" Authentication scheme (with an Authorization header), and not the Signature HTTP header, is used for signature.
[Required Headers]
This section describes the headers that must be included in the signing string.
For GET and DELETE requests (when there's no content in the request body), the signing string must include at least these headers:
- host (as host:port in case of port different from 80, 443)
- date (in RFC 1123)
- (request-target) (as described in https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-cavage-http-signatures-10)
 For PUT and POST requests (when there's content in the request body), the signing string must include at least these headers:
- host (as host:port in case of port different from 80, 443)
- date (in RFC 1123)
- (request-target) (as described in https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-cavage-http-signatures-10)
- digest 'SHA-256=' + (BASE64 encoded string of the SHA-256 from request body) (ex. SHA-256=6iJfkOF3ra8+t09DtcpwjR6Kxt6lnv+aF5GtzZm6ue0=)
 For multipart/form-data requests, the signing string must include at least these headers:
- host (as host:port in case of port different from 80, 443)
- date (in RFC 1123)
- (request-target) (as described in https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-cavage-http-signatures-10)
 [URL Encoding of Path and Query String]
When forming the signing string, you must URL encode all parameters in the path and query string (but not the headers) according to RFC 3986.
[Key Identifier]
You must set keyId in the Authorization header with the same value of the merId in the request.
[Signing Algorithm]
The signing algorithm must be HMAC-SHA256, and you must set algorithm="hmac-sha256" in the Authorization header (notice the quotation marks).
[Example Header]
Here's an example of the general syntax of the Authorization header (for a request with content in the body):
Authorization: Signature keyId="${merId}",algorithm="hmac-sha256",headers="host date (request-target) digest",signature="${Base64(HMAC-SHA256(signing_string))}"
For signing string specification look at https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-cavage-http-signatures-10

Sample Code
This section shows the basic code for signing API requests.
- JAVA (https://github.com/tomitribe/http-signatures-java)
- PHP (https://github.com/99designs/http-signatures-php)
- RUBY (https://github.com/99designs/http-signatures-ruby)

payload.description:
Object contains Raw Payment payload, different for Payment Instrument

For ApplePay:
- Raw 'Payment Token' returned by ApplePay during payment validation

For GooglePay:
- Raw 'Payment Token' returned by GooglePay during payment validation

For AmazonPay:
- JSON object containing following parameters returned by AmazonPay:
{
"amazonOrderReferenceId": "OrderID"
"accessToken": "AccessToken"
}

For WeChat:
- JSON object containing following parameters:
{
"trade_type": "Transaction Type: JSAPI or NATIVE"
"openid": "User unique identifier, this field is only required when trade_type is JSAPI"
}

For PCIpal:
- JSON object containing following parameters:
{
  "encData": "Base64 Cipher RSA/ECB/PKCS1Padding PlainCard ",
  "version": "IGFS_2",
  "publicKeyHash": "Base64 SHA-256 of the X509 encode public key"
}
